questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a location where I could receive a good education (in English), but preferably in a country that spoke another language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Didn't know how to access Brightspace and had to figure it out myself. The same with other apps needed for the university, but most of the information I needed was available online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had the chance to attend a orientation week (which I did and cost me 100 euro).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They didn't provide anything beside showing me the city and where the university was located and stuff like that...

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was terrible. Students who want to study in the Netherlands should honestly get a warning that it's going to be incredibly difficult to find housing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's gonna be a bit more expensive, unless you live in biking-distance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: NOT. ENOUGH. HOUSING. FOR. STUDENTS.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You found a course you like, write down the code and send it to them (more or less)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had websites which showed how to interpret the different systems (EC and level)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful at all! I wanted some masters courses which they didn't allow me to attend, due to the fact that I was a bachelor-student... Even though my home university would've and did allow me to

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the levels + EC (to make sure you can get the course) and don't take more than 4 courses!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was wildly different depending on the course. Disregarding the introductory courses I had, it seemed that the more complex the course, the less coherent the course became. The academic level was high, but the teaching level didn't always keep up

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was lacking to say the least. Linguistics on UCPH is blessed with great and talented teachers and professors, so the bar was high and the host university did not pass it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Languages of the World
Speech sounds of the World
Language Documentation
Religion in the World
Violence and the brain
Introduction to Psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Speech sounds of the World was the best course I had by far! Talented professor with funny classes, and good ways to practice!

Violence and the brain was also interesting, but very short!

questions.answer: Public transport was really expensive!!!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basically all kinds of student associations... You could find one for every kind of person

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find friends or people on your courses that seem nice and hang out with them. They might be your new best friend!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Relax!!! Do everything at your own pace. And if you want: go see the country! Public transport is expensive, but the infrastructure in the Netherlands is really good

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Extremely easy: Danish and Dutch culture are much alike

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They didn't have big beers :C

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *

questions.answer: Try to find out how Brightspace works! :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: FINDING HOUSING
